cases.reason: The closing paragraph of 14.5.12.1.2 is word-identical to 2023's. 2023's clause adds items (SORT/MERGE, fatal EC-I-O, PERFORM WHEN, APPLY COMMIT ROLLBACK) about dispositions, not about compile-time detection. No communication or debugging reach.

scope-2002: native arithmetic size error without a phrase, checking off (receivers keep low-order digits, execution continues)
zero divisor / exponentiation violation / unformable intermediate with checking off (termination)
2002 STANDARD arithmetic: a standard intermediate outside 10^-999..10^1000-10^968 is EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW/UNDERFLOW (§2002:8.8.1.3.1 rule 2), fatal; disposition with checking off
evidence-2002: native arms covered at --std 2002: pb77_move_past_the_carrier, pb3975_remainder_after_quotient_size_error, pb4031_report_source_size_checking, pb4031_report_overflow_checking, pb4092_size_checking_is_per_name, pb4093_truncation_not_enabled_stores_low_order_digits, pb4092_report_compose_per_name, pb639_store_landing_low_order_digits_2002, pb640_call/invoke_argument_landing_checked_2002, pb3869_not_size_error_alone, pb4640 (all MATCH, cases-50-51.log, cases-51b.log); pb129, pb3990 x2, pb4031_prohibited (ROUNDED MODE, 2014 form) and pb75 / pb3975_standard_decimal (STANDARD-DECIMAL, 2014 form) refused at 2002 as they should be
standard-arithmetic arm NOT shown, and wrong: probe p51_std_overflow.cob

citations.quote: how any receiving operands are affected when events that would cause a fatal exception to exist occur but checking for that condition is not enabled
If checking for the exception condition is not enabled, the implementor defines whether or not execution will continue, how it will continue, and how any receiving operands are affected
If checking for the exception condition is not enabled, the implementor defines whether or not execution will continue, how it will continue, and how any receiving operands are affected
The size error condition is raised and the EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW or EC-SIZE-UNDERFLOW exception condition is set to exist if the value is too large or too small
with a precision of 32 decimal digits

cases.reason: Rule 5 of 2002 is 2023's item 8 without the APPLY COMMIT sentence. In 2002 the fatal conditions this item governs include the standard intermediate's overflow under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD (32 digits, 10^-999 to 10^1000-10^968), a form the 2023 row never shows (its standard arm is STANDARD-DECIMAL, a 2014 form refused at 2002). DOC-A.1-70's determination says an intermediate that cannot be formed terminates the run unit with checking off. Probe at --std 2002: OPTIONS ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD, B=10, E=1001, R PIC 9(5) VALUE 7, COMPUTE R = B ** E with no phrase: prints AFTER R=00000, exit 0. 10^1001 exceeds 2002's standard intermediate, so EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW exists; the compiler never raises it (it carries decimal128) and stores low-order digits. This is the known PB5575 (2002 standard arithmetic uses 2014's 34-digit decimal128 model, range included) reaching this row, not a new defect.
cases.needs: its own verdict: the compiler's behaviour at --std 2002 for a standard-arithmetic intermediate overflow with checking off is continue with low-order digits (no EC raised); a 2002 witness after PB5575
cases.compiler-at-2002: wrong (probe E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/op-20261114/read-2002/out/probes-u-39/p51_std_overflow.cob, log p51_std_overflow.log; known defect PB5575, expected: EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW per §2002:8.8.1.3.1 rule 2 and then the documented unchecked disposition, termination)

cases.reason: 8.5.1.5.1 governs the start of EVERY alphanumeric group item. In 2002 the record description entries following a CD entry are alphanumeric groups that implicitly redefine the CD record area (A.1.1.2; A.1.2.2 SR5/SR9/SR14), and the compiler implements the communication section at --std 2002 (warning COBOL0903 only). The row's witnesses (l1c01_group_start_coincident, l1c01_group_start_typed_national_bit) show only working-storage groups, so the CD-record part of the 2002 scope has no evidence through the 2023 row. Probe r6_cd_group_start.cob at --std 2002: an output CD with 01 CREC (CA X(4), CB X(4)) and 01 CRE2 X(8); MOVE 'ABCDEFGH' TO CRE2 gives CA=ABCD CB=EFGH, lengths 8 8: the group start coincides with its first item, as documented. Compiler correct; the probe is a candidate 2002 witness.

cases.reason: 2002 14.5.8 rule 2 governs every receiving item described as floating-point numeric. In 2002 a user record under an output CD may contain FLOAT-SHORT/LONG/EXTENDED items (no Annex A rule restricts usage there), and such an item may be a receiving operand; the compiler accepts this at --std 2002. The row's witness pb1110_float_short_every_landing receives only into working-storage items, so the CD-record receiving operand (the reach u-34 overturned for item 1's ACCEPT identifier-1) has no evidence through the 2023 row. Probe r7_61_cd_items.cob at --std 2002: FLOAT-LONG CFL in a CD record; COMPUTE CFL = 1 / 3 equals the working-storage twin, MOVE 123.25 TO CFL compares equal to 123.25. Compiler correct; candidate 2002 witness. (The reader's own note stands: 2002 leaves the alignment wholly to the implementor where 2023 requires the algebraic value; the determination lies inside 2002's latitude.)

cases.reason: 2002 licenses non-support by processor dependence: B.3 item 1 makes the whole screen section processor-dependent and 3.1.5 lets an implementation not claim it; the compiler refuses every screen-section construct at --std 2002 (COBOL1560 on the section header and on FOREGROUND-COLOR), so it claims no part of it and the B.1 preamble withdraws the item. Only the diagnostic's wording (it cites 2023's A.4.2 licence at 2002) differs; that is not a requirement difference.

cases.reason: Conditionally required in both; the condition (non-COBOL function activation) is absent at 2002 as at 2023 and the absence witness runs at 2002. 2023's function-pointer-name-1 is a widening.

The item governs the result whenever a 2002 function's argument rules are violated with checking off, so it defers to every function's argument rules, and those differ. 2002 NUMVAL caps argument-1 at 31 digits UNCONDITIONALLY (AR1 'one to 31 digits', AR2), including under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD; 2023 caps 31 only under native arithmetic and allows 34 under standard-decimal. Probe r69_numval_std.cob at --std 2002 with OPTIONS ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD: FUNCTION NUMVAL of a 33-digit string returns +1234567890123456789012345.678901 (the value), not the documented default 0; the native twin r69_numval_nat.cob returns 0 as documented. So at --std 2002 a violation of a 2002 argument rule is not detected under standard arithmetic and the implementor-defined result is not produced. The row's witnesses run native only. This is the PB5575 family (2002 standard arithmetic modelled on 2014's 34-digit decimal) reaching this row; the same 31-digit cap stands in 2002 NUMVAL-C and NUMVAL-F (not probed).
